echo: Our emails aren’t turning enough subscribers into buyers.
intro: There was a time when more email subscribers meant more money. **That time has passed.** Now three things decide whether email becomes your most profitable channel:
t1: Why a subscriber joins your list
t1s: to diagnose a real problem, not grab a freebie
t2: How many buy in the first 14 days
t3: How many non-buyers and buyers buy after the first 14 days
t3s: lifecycle emails, not one newsletter pool
p1_h1: We sent the #1 SDR Sales Coach’s exact same emails to two of his lists. The 10,000 subscribers list he built by sharing a freebie a week made 1 sale, and his Conversion Quiz™ list pulled {{23 sales.}}
p1_context: The #1 SDR Sales Coach had built a list of 10,000 subscribers with “Comment X, Get Y” posts, and his emails weren’t converting despite every effort. So we sent the exact same sequence, with the same messaging and the same timing, to two lists at once.
why: the only difference was the frame they joined with. People who joined to diagnose a real gap were far more likely to buy the fix than people who just wanted a quick freebie.
next1: So what happens after they join?
p2_h1: Lara Acosta’s first launch sold only 30 seats, but two launches after we rebuilt her email strategy, she sold {{500 seats}}.
p2_context: Lara Acosta, Forbes 30 Under 30 and the number one female LinkedIn creator, was gaining subscribers fast from her 180,000+ followers, but her first launch drew only 30 students and a 6% click-through rate.
built_1: A pre-launch, launch and post-launch email strategy that shifted beliefs before asking for the sale
built_2: Affiliate collaborations and a masterclass layered on top
built_3: Behaviour-triggered sequences that compounded with every launch
p2_r1s: email is now the most profitable channel in her business
up_next: Next question: Where does most of your traffic or audience come from today?
quad: Making each subscriber more profitable month on month falls under Quadrant # 4 of the Compounding Revenue Per Visitor™ OS.
